prompt: Customers say the orders dashboard froze at 06:41 UTC. It reads from replica db-orders-r2 (MySQL 8.0.36). The Grafana 'Replication Lag' panel for r2 has shown a flat 0s all morning, yet rows committed on source db-orders-p1 after 06:41 never appear on r2. On-call suspects app-level caching. Determine where replication actually stands and restore data flow.

PagerDuty at 03:53 UTC: replication on db-billing-r1 (8.0.34) has been stopped since 03:12 with Last_SQL_Errno 1062, duplicate entry '882441' for key 'invoices.PRIMARY'. Source db-billing-p1 is healthy and writing. r1 serves all invoice reads, now 41 minutes stale and aging. Get the applier running again and establish how the duplicate got there.

db-catalog-r3 (8.0.37) reconnected this morning after a 2-day network migration and alerted at 07:55: Last_IO_Errno 1236, 'Got fatal error from source: Could not find first log file name in binary log index file'. Source db-catalog-p1 writes roughly 40 one-GB binlogs per day and the dataset is ~800GB. Recover replication on r3.

Planned failover of db-users-p1 for a kernel patch aborted at 21:20: orchestrator refuses to promote db-users-r2, reporting an errant GTID on it. r2 shows lag 0 and clean threads, and the maintenance window closes at 22:00. Identify the errant transaction, reconcile it safely, and get r2 promoted inside the window.

Nightly reconciliation flagged loyalty-points divergence: totals for roughly 40k users differ between db-loyalty-p1 and replica db-loyalty-r1. Replication monitoring is green — lag under 1s all week, zero SQL errors. Both run 8.0.35 with legacy binlog_format=STATEMENT. Support is crediting users by hand. Find why the replica diverged and repair it end to end.

Post-incident review: last night's 02:12 emergency failover from db-pay-p1 to db-pay-r1 lost 3 committed payment transactions despite semi-sync replication being our stated zero-loss guarantee (8.0.36, rpl_semi_sync_source_timeout=10000). The cluster failed back to p1 at 06:10; finance rebuilt the missing rows from app logs. No semi-sync alert ever fired. Determine why durability degraded silently and restore the guarantee.

Marketplace sellers report ~5% of profile edits disappear on the next page load and reappear about a minute later, worst at traffic peaks. Stack: ProxySQL 2.6 in front of db-mkt-p1 with read replicas r1/r2 (8.0.36); the lag panel shows a 0.11s average. Make read-your-writes hold for the profile edit flow.

Since yesterday's replica tuning on db-feed-r4 (8.0.35, replica_parallel_workers raised 4 to 16), the feed service intermittently reads comment rows whose parent post is missing; a retry one second later succeeds. About 200 anomalies per hour at peak, replica only — source data is fine. Explain the inversion on r4 and stop it without giving up parallel apply.

A hypervisor crash at 04:18 hard-reset db-search-r2 (8.0.34). mysqld came back and the 'replication connected' check is green, but r2's newest document row is still from 04:17 and the 60-second search-freshness SLO is burning. Source db-search-p1 keeps 7 days of binlogs. Get r2 applying again and explain the green check.

Replica db-wh-r1 (8.0.33, replicate-do-db=warehouse, fleet-wide binlog_format=STATEMENT) shows zero rows in warehouse.stock_rollup for 2026-07-02 while source db-wh-p1 has 86,400; other warehouse tables are current and replication reports no errors, lag 0. The rollup is written nightly at 02:00 by a batch job. Find where the rows vanish and fix their replication.

Since an 11:30 ProxySQL config push, storefront inventory counts are exactly one hour stale for a fraction of requests. Reads flow through ProxySQL 2.5 to the db-inv fleet (8.0.36: source p1, replicas r1, r2, plus DR host r-delay). The fleet lag dashboard shows every replica green under 1s. Find why reads are stale and fix the routing.

db-ledger-r1 (8.0.37, 16 parallel applier workers) alerted at 02:00: Seconds_Behind_Source 2,410 and climbing roughly 55s per minute since 01:20. Source db-ledger-p1 traffic is normal, no schema changes deployed. Downstream freshness checks on ledger reads are failing. Diagnose the stall and get lag back to zero safely.

db-geo-r3 (8.0.35) paged at 05:02: error log repeating 'Disk is full writing ./relay-bin.003021 (OS errno 28 - No space left on device); waiting for someone to free some space'. The node dashboard shows the server at 41% disk used. The replica is 6,800s behind and climbing. Free space safely, restore replication, and explain the buildup.

Automated failover at 02:40 promoted db-auth-r1 to source after a kernel panic on db-auth-p1; orchestrator reports the topology healthy and p1 rejoined as a replica at 03:02. Since then auth-api INSERT and UPDATE calls fail with MySQL error 1290 'running with --super-read-only' — about 35% of requests. ProxySQL 2.6 fronts the fleet. Stop the write failures.
